atlas-no.0070: NBIM’s 12-month graduate programme starts with nine months on the AI team and three in a business area, and asks for a completed bachelor’s, master’s, MBA or PhD and up to two years of work experience.
atlas-no.0071: Auditing and consulting have long been the largest destinations of NHH graduates, and the Big Four make offers to students a year before they finish, after a summer internship.
atlas-no.0072: BCG takes visiting associates for a six-week internship that can lead to a full-time role; EY and Accenture ran company courses at the NHH career fair.
atlas-no.0073: Equinor’s graduate programme lasts two years with rotations and gives full Equinor employment with the benefits of the country of work; Aker BP’s offers permanent positions and relocation help to graduates from outside Norway.
atlas-no.0074: NBIM’s 2027 graduate programme is built around its AI team and asks for enthusiasm for AI and a sincere interest in finance; selection includes an AI case-study exercise.
atlas-no.0075: Recent tech graduates report a harder market as consultancies hire fewer juniors, but DNB still runs a graduate programme for developers, IT architects and cybersecurity, and Equinor recruits IT and cybernetics graduates; NTNU in Trondheim is the main source.
atlas-no.0076: DNB’s graduate programme includes a cybersecurity track, with applications closing on 1 October.
atlas-no.0077: Public employers advertise through Jobbnorge, a board run by Grade Jobbnorge AS that also sells recruitment tools to employers; Nav’s Arbeidsplassen lists public and private posts.
atlas-no.0078: The programmes recruit once a year in the autumn or late summer: NBIM took applications from 1 to 15 August 2026, DNB’s IT and cybersecurity programme closed on 1 October, and campus career days fall in September.
atlas-no.0079: NBIM accepts a bachelor’s, master’s, MBA or PhD, completed before the start, and the business-school pipeline is a master’s (NHH’s class is surveyed six months after the master’s).
atlas-no.0080: HK-dir, the Norwegian ENIC-NARIC centre, handles foreign-education recognition; not all professions require recognition, but regulated professions need authorisation or recognition of the professional qualifications.
atlas-no.0081: Firms visit NHH, BI and NTNU, and NHH’s fair has close to 100 companies, but the programmes read name no list of schools and NBIM takes a bachelor’s to a PhD.
atlas-no.0082: The entry for business and engineering students is the summer internship and the programme after the master’s; the sources read show no apprenticeship or dual-study route for graduates.
atlas-no.0083: Public employers advertise on Jobbnorge and Nav’s Arbeidsplassen; the large graduate programmes read are at a sovereign-wealth manager, a bank and energy groups.
atlas-no.0084: Aker BP offers graduates from universities outside Norway relocation help, immigration and work-permit support and language training; NBIM works in English and does not require Norwegian. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-no.0085: A photo is optional on a Norwegian CV; the guide read advises one A4 page, two at most.
atlas-no.0086: Aim for one A4 page, two at most, with a clear layout since paper CVs may be scanned; write in Norwegian for Norwegian postings and in English for English ones, and technology, oil and gas may prefer English.
atlas-no.0087: Most employers expect a cover letter tailored to the company and its industry; if you are not fluent in Norwegian, state your willingness to learn it.
atlas-no.0088: Expat.com lists references among the items on the CV and calls them highly important in spontaneous applications; other guides differ on whether to list them or wait until asked.
atlas-no.0089: A spontaneous application should include a complete CV and your diplomas; the online programme applications read ask for a CV and academic records rather than certified copies.
atlas-no.0090: Norway has no national minimum wage and many industries set minimum pay through collective agreements; the application pages read ask for a CV and letter, not a salary figure.
atlas-no.0091: Expat.com calls references highly important and Equinor’s selection includes an online assessment and video interview; no source read describes background or criminal-record checks for graduates.
atlas-no.0092: Applications through structured programmes and advertised posts work; elsewhere, many jobs are filled through referrals, and contacts made during the internship decide.
atlas-no.0093: Equinor’s selection runs through an online application, online assessment, video interview and a virtual recruitment day; NBIM’s adds online assessments and an AI case study, with online or in-person interviews, and takes documents in English or Norwegian.
atlas-no.0094: Norwegian for most roles outside global energy, tech and consulting teams; many Norwegians speak English, but Norwegian is often required for permanent roles and career advancement, while NBIM’s working language is English.
atlas-no.0095: Equinor’s graduate selection has five steps: online application, online assessment, video interview, virtual recruitment day, then the offer. NBIM’s has five too: CV screening, online assessments (personality profile and psychometric tests), an AI case study, interviews online or in person, then the offer.
atlas-no.0096: Ordinary interviews are straightforward and professional, with questions on experience, technical skills, teamwork, motivation and long-term commitment; punctuality is important.
atlas-no.0097: Dress is professional but modest: creative and tech sectors are more casual, while finance and law expect business attire.
atlas-no.0098: The first step can be very selective: DNB’s summer internship drew close to 500 applications for ten places.
atlas-no.0099: A written contract is mandatory: for employment over one month it must be ready no later than seven days after the start, and a contract cannot set a shorter notice period than the Working Environment Act requires.
atlas-no.0100: A trial period normally lasts up to six months; during it either side gives 14 days’ notice unless otherwise agreed in writing, and afterwards the statutory notice is one month under five years of service, two months over five and three to six months over ten.
atlas-no.0101: Holiday is at least 25 working days a year (Saturdays count, so four weeks and one day); some collective agreements add a fifth week, and the holiday pay rate then rises from 10.2% to 12%.
atlas-no.0102: There is no national minimum wage; collective agreements set minimum pay in many industries. NHH’s 2025 master’s class had a median gross salary of NOK 600,000 for those working in Norway; Equinor’s graduates are full employees with the benefits of the country of work.
atlas-no.0103: Aker BP says graduates from universities outside Norway get relocation help, covering travel costs, housing search, a first-year housing allowance, immigration and work-permit support and language training.
atlas-no.0104: NBIM says English is the working language across the organisation and Norwegian is not required, and application documents can be in English or Norwegian; its page does not mention permits.
atlas-no.0105: Work-visa processing can take several weeks, so ask the employer about permits at the offer stage; the pay floors for a skilled-worker permit are in Visas. No source read describes a labour-market test or a quota.
atlas-no.0106: Posted vacancies: Nav’s Arbeidsplassen (a service from Nav that also links to EURES), FINN.no and Jobbnorge for public employers; Nav’s board can be filtered for English by searching “English”.
atlas-no.0107: Graduate programmes: NBIM, Equinor and Aker BP post theirs on their own career pages, DNB on jobb.dnb.no; Work in Norway offers an employer database and practical information.
atlas-no.0108: University fairs: BI’s Karrieredagene in Oslo every autumn (about 100 companies), NHH’s career fair in Bergen in September, and NTNU’s career service and career days in Trondheim.
atlas-no.0109: Agencies: Manpower, Experis and Adecco focus on tech, engineering and finance.
atlas-no.0110: Missing the late-summer and autumn windows: NBIM’s 2027 round ran from 1 to 15 August 2026, and DNB’s IT and cybersecurity programme closed on 1 October.
atlas-no.0111: Skipping the summer internship: Big Four offers to NHH students come a year before they finish, after a summer internship.
atlas-no.0112: Sending a long CV or leaving out references: aim for one A4 page, two at most, and expect to be asked for references.
atlas-no.0113: Sending a Norwegian CV for an English-language posting, or the reverse: write in the language of the ad, and say you are willing to learn Norwegian if you are not fluent.
atlas-no.0114: Applying to Aker BP without an advertised position: it accepts applications only for advertised positions.
atlas-no.0115: NBIM’s working language is English across the organisation, Norwegian is not required and documents can be in English or Norwegian; no certificate is named, the online assessments and interviews are the evidence.
atlas-no.0116: Aker BP’s graduate page is in English and offers language training to graduates from outside Norway; Expat.com says Norwegian is often required for permanent roles and career advancement.
atlas-no.0117: Technology, oil and gas may prefer an English CV because English is the main working language there; Nav’s board has English-language postings.
atlas-no.0118: NBIM’s AI-team graduate programme works in English and asks for no Norwegian.
atlas-no.0119: Public employers advertise on Jobbnorge in Norwegian; the sources read name no English route, so expect to need Norwegian.
atlas-no.0120: NHH’s survey is answered by 193 of 660 master’s graduates (36%), so its NOK 600,000 median is a self-selected figure for those working in Norway; the 2024 median was NOK 580,000.
atlas-no.0121: 91.8% of recent tertiary graduates were in work in 2025, among Europe’s strongest rates, while youth unemployment (15 to 24) was 14.0% and rising from 11.0% in 2023; no source read gives a return-offer rate for Norwegian summer internships.
atlas-no.0122: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens may work from the first day under the EEA agreement; a delay in getting a police appointment does not make the stay irregular.
